text:
Roope Hintz is quietly having one of the more valuable seasons in the league. By our wins-added measure he ranks 41st of 568 skaters, and his 23 points in 25 games come with real chances behind them: Dallas controls 52% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice.

The finishing is running hot. He's scoring on 20% of his shots, well above the 12 to 16% range we'd expect from him, so the goal pace may slow even if the underlying game doesn't. His last ten games have been more playmaker than shooter anyway: 7 assists, 3 goals.

The tools are as loud as ever. NHL EDGE has him in the 99th percentile for bursts over 20 mph, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 63% of his entries last season. Evolving-Hockey rated him 20th among all forwards in 2025-26 and elite at suppressing chances. When a forward at 16 and a half minutes a night does all that, it's worth noticing.
